virality_data.topic: Building an ADHD-Friendly AI Coding Skill to Stop Agent Context Dumps
virality_data.analysis: Agent verbosity and context burying is the single biggest productivity bottleneck developers face when using autonomous coding tools today. Strong cross-source momentum across Hacker News (296 comments) and GitHub trending validates massive community frustration with multi-agent chatter. This article stands out by providing a concise, copy-pasteable skill script that forces agents to extract actionable diffs instead of hiding solutions in walls of text.
cross_source_signals: Hacker News #2 cluster: 296 comments on 'I-have-ADHD: A skill to stop coding agents from burying the answer'
Developer community discourse around agent tool-call verbosity and context optimization
virality_data.story_angle: I spent three hours debugging a broken auth middleware because my autonomous coding agent buried the critical 2-line fix inside an 800-word architectural monologue.
virality_data.suman_angle: How I Built a 40-Line Skill That Stops Coding Agents From Hiding the Fix
virality_data.competing_articles: Most agent skill tutorials teach how to add more tools; this post teaches how to restrain agent output and surface immediate diffs with working code.

virality_data.topic: Automating Multi-Format Document Ingestion by Building an In-Browser WASM Parser
virality_data.analysis: Document preparation and academic typesetting workflows are notoriously fragile, requiring heavy backend compute or expensive SaaS subscriptions. The high engagement on browser-based compilation (118 points on HN) proves that devs want client-side, zero-server document pipelines. This guide provides a practical blueprint for automating document compiling directly in the client without server infrastructure costs.
